speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started, and have you had any recent injuries or bites to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the finger look dislocated or bent at an unusual angle, and are you able to fully bend and straighten it? I also need to know if you have any numbness or tingling sensations in the fingertip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint and the avulsion mechanism, this is highly suggestive of a "Jersey Finger" injury. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a "Jersey Finger" injury with an avulsion mechanism and inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint is classic for a flexor digitorum profundus tendon rupture. The negative X-ray rules out bony avulsion, confirming a soft tissue tendon injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Profundus Tendon Rupture

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
